faq: Is homemade kimchi hard or scary to make?

The author says making kimchi really is very easy, not at all scary, and delicious. The recipe came from watching videos and reading recipes online and combining the best ideas, ratios and methods, so he encourages experimenting; The Art of Fermentation by Sandor Katz is the book he recommends on safety, equipment and styles.
Is this kimchi vegetarian?

Yes. Most store kimchi contains seafood like anchovy sauce, fish sauce or dried shrimp for umami. This recipe omits them and uses only a small amount of soy sauce (gluten-free soy sauce if you want gluten-free kimchi).
How long does kimchi take to ferment?

Store it covered in a cool, dark place, tasting and tossing daily. It starts to develop a pleasing acidity and is ripe to your taste anywhere from 3 days up to a couple of weeks, then transfer to clean jars and refrigerate.
Should the container be sealed tight?
No. Cover it but allow a little airflow, because a tight lid can be blown off by CO2. The author's coworker rigged an airlock on a cambro.
How do you brine the cabbage?

Whisk 1 liter of water with 150 grams of kosher salt (Diamond Crystal) in a very clean container, submerge the cabbage, cover and weight it for about 1 hour until tender and well-seasoned, then drain thoroughly.
Can I add MSG or yeast extract for more umami?

The author's tests mixing MSG or yeast extracts into partly fermented kimchi tasted quite good. If you experiment, try about 0.5% of the total weight (0.1% for pure MSG). Kombu and dried shiitake also have free glutamates.
What do I serve kimchi with?
Kimchi fried rice, tofu and kimchi dinner for one, bibim naengmyeon, or the kimchi jigae in the cookbook.

summary: Fingerling potatoes, chanterelles and shallots cooked about 8 minutes in butter, simmered tender with a little water, then finished with a red wine pan sauce mounted with butter; serves 2 as a major side.
glance: 2 as a major side or up to 4 as a few bites
about 8 minutes browning, then simmer until the potatoes are tender
3/4 cup red wine, deglazed and whisked with butter
yield: 2 as a major side or up to 4 as a few bites
faq: What potatoes and mushrooms work here?

The author used heirloom Rose Finn fingerling potatoes (small or cut fingerlings) and plump, firm chanterelles, thoroughly wiped clean. He chose them because the chanterelles at the co-op were plump and firm and not dried up or soggy.
How do you make the red wine pan sauce?

Remove the cooked vegetables, deglaze the pan with 3/4 cup of red wine over medium-high heat scraping up the browned bits (the fond), then vigorously whisk in the remaining butter so the sauce has a nice sheen. It takes just a couple of minutes.
How do you cook the potatoes?

Brown them with the chanterelles, shallots, rosemary and salt in 2 tablespoons of butter for about 8 minutes, add 1/2 cup water, cover and simmer until tender, adding water as needed, then remove the lid and cook off any remaining liquid.
What does it taste like?
Ridiculously simple, earthy, rich and delicious, with a very French feel. The author likes to mash the potatoes into the leftover sauce and mop it all up.
Is the dish gluten-free?
Yes, it is vegetarian and gluten-free as written.
